matches.quote: Fig. 4c shows the ππ intra-band channel dominating −Im χ⁰ from ~0.5 to 1.5 eV... show the Fig. 4c decomposition at several q with the Eq. 32 orbital weighting
The tight-binding bands (Fig. S3) deviate visibly from DFT along A–L–H and for one σ band near Γ–A close to E_F; comment on the effect on the Lindhard function
The authors should show an incident-energy RIXS map across the pre-edge at one or two fixed q to demonstrate a constant (Raman-like) energy loss
unclear whether the Lindhard and RPA calculations (Figs. 3d, 3e, 4) used the actual (q_∥, q_⊥) of each spectrum or only q_∥ along Γ–M with q_⊥ = 0
The feature is "markedly asymmetric"... compare full lineshapes and widths with resolution-convolved χ⁰/χ (with and without RPA) at each measured (q_∥, q_⊥), on a common intensity scale
The novelty claims are overstated... particle-hole continua have been compared with Lindhard-type calculations in RIXS and momentum-resolved EELS of metallic oxides, including Ref. 23.
The statement that EELS "cannot see" low-energy intra-band excitations (p. 5) is derived for a single-component system... soften the "cannot see" wording accordingly.
show... the Γ–K data mentioned in SI Sec. A but never shown (... so Γ–M versus Γ–K is a consistency check).

notes: C7 is marked partly raised by P21, which identifies the 0.5-1.5 eV feature in Fig. 4c (a cut of Fig. 3d) as the pi-pi intraband channel and asks to apply the Eq. 32 polarization/orbital weighting across q to explain its suppression relative to the sigma states. C10 is marked partly raised by P6 and P7, which challenge the overly broad sum-rule claim that EELS/IXS cannot see the continuum and ask to qualify it (via the plasmon cutoff and multiband screening nuances rather than low-density/semimetal regimes). C5 is marked not raised because while P8/P19 question the polarization explanation of the angle dependence, they ask for sigma-polarized RIXS and self-absorption checks rather than complementary XAS data.
